honorific: Forms of address, syntax and prose cadence guidance (en→zh): translate English into idiomatic, fluent Chinese rather than word-for-word translationese. Break long hypotactic English sentences with nested relative clauses and participial modifiers into crisp, natural Chinese clauses instead of stacking multiple '的' modifiers or passive '被' constructions. Preserve rhetorical balance, irony, antithesis and formal vs. colloquial register. Render titles and honorifics (Mr., Mrs., Miss, Lord, Lady, Sir, Dr., Majesty, Excellency) naturally and consistently by speaker-to-listener relationship. Standardize transliterated Western personal names with consistent middle-dot spacing (·) and preserve established Chinese renderings of well-known historical figures, institutions and places. Format quoted epigraphs and verse with explicit line breaks (\n) and clean Chinese punctuation.
